summary: Vegetarian. Firm tofu, cubed and dusted with cornflour, cooked until the outside is dry and crisp while the middle stays soft. About 20 minutes end to end, and the washing-up is one bowl and the basket.

ingredients.note: Silken tofu collapses here. Firm or extra-firm is the one to buy.
Plain flour works and gives a softer crust; rice flour crisps hardest.
Contains soy, and wheat unless the bottle says gluten free.

ingredients.item: Garlic powder, smoked paprika or five-spice
ingredients.note: Whichever jar is already in the cupboard; the method does not change.

method.instruction: Pat the tofu dry with a clean tea towel, cut it into cubes of about 2 cm, and toss it in a bowl with the soy sauce first, then the oil, then the cornflour and spice. This order helps the coating stick evenly and reduces clumping.
Set the air fryer to 200°C. Preheat only if your appliance manual tells you to; many models do not need it.
Spread the cubes in the basket in a single layer with a little space around each one. Baskets differ in size, so if yours is full, cook in two batches rather than piling the tofu up.

Cook for 12 to 14 minutes, shaking at about 7 minutes. Dry, firm, golden edges are texture cues only. Treat tofu as ready to eat only if its package explicitly permits it; otherwise follow its cooking instructions, which override this starting time.

After cooking, switch off, unplug and let the appliance cool before cleaning. Follow its manual for removable parts, soaking and cleaning products; never immerse the electrical unit or assume water alone is enough.

yield_note: Two servings as a main with rice, or four as a side. Preparation and cooking together take about 20 minutes. Editorial measuring convention for these original notes: tablespoon 20 mL; teaspoon 5 mL. These are volume measures, not gram conversions.

caveats: Check the tofu packet for ready-to-eat status. Follow any required cooking instructions and the stated refrigerated storage and use-by directions after opening.
The basket, drawer and escaping air can be very hot. Use handles and oven mitts as directed by the manual and set removable parts on a heatproof surface.
Allergens: soy in the tofu and in the soy sauce, plus wheat in most soy sauce. Check your bottle’s ingredient and allergen labels.
These are practical notes, not tested or safety-reviewed. This project has not cooked this recipe, and the timings are a starting point for your own machine rather than a verified result.
